classification.difficultyReason: Inspect each supplied graph for y-axis reflection and origin rotational symmetry, selecting neither when both tests fail; no equation reconstruction or algebra is required.

content.prompt: Classify the following graphs as either even, odd or neither.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex at the axes' intersection, arrowheads on both upper ends, no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Reflection symmetry across the y-axis. The source gives no equation or numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible. Its classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Even, because the graph is symmetric across the $y$-axis.

spec.description: Increasing S-curve through the origin, horizontal tangent there, lower-left and upper-right arrowheads. Axes have no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Rotational symmetry of 180 degrees about the origin. No equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible. Its classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Odd, because the graph has rotational symmetry of $180^\circ$ about the origin.

spec.description: Positive increasing exponential-shaped curve approaching the horizontal axis to the left and crossing the vertical axis above the origin. Arrowheads at both ends, no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: The curve has neither y-axis reflection symmetry nor origin rotational symmetry. No equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is always visible. Its classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Neither. The graph has neither reflection symmetry across the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry of $180^\circ$ about the origin.

spec.description: Upper unit semicircle with closed endpoints at (-1,0) and (1,0), peak at (0,1), labelled axes and the three printed numerical values. No grid or curve-extension arrows.
spec.mathematics: Upper semicircle x²+y²=1 with y nonnegative. Equal horizontal and vertical units preserve the circle.
spec.answerVisibility: All endpoints and printed values are permanent givens. The classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Even, because the graph is symmetric across the $y$-axis.

spec.description: Decreasing inverse-cosine-shaped curve with closed endpoints (-1,π) and (1,0), dashed guides from the upper endpoint to both axes, x values -1 and 1, and y value π. No curve-extension arrows or grid.
spec.mathematics: The inverse-cosine-shaped graph has positive vertical-axis intercept and lacks both required symmetries. The parameterisation preserves the supplied endpoints and shape without displaying an equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve, guides, endpoints and values are permanent givens. The classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Neither. The graph has neither reflection symmetry across the $y$-axis nor rotational symmetry of $180^\circ$ about the origin.

spec.description: Smooth positive symmetric bell-shaped curve with peak (0,1), outward arrowheads on both tails and labelled axes. Only the peak value 1 is printed. No grid.
spec.mathematics: Reflection symmetry across the y-axis. The source supplies no equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph and peak value remain visible. The classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: Even, because the graph is symmetric across the $y$-axis.
